Respiratory system
Children with obesity have a considerably higher prevalence of OSA than do normal-weight children. The prevalence and severity of
OSA increase with increasing BMI. Children with severe obesity may also have alveolar hypoventilation associated with severe
oxygen desaturation. Childhood obesity has also been shown to be associated with asthma (Kumar and Kelly, 2017; Poskitt,
2013; Styne et al., 2017).
Gastrointestinal system
Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in children is strongly associated with obesity. The spectrum of NAFLD can range from
simple steatosis to progressive steatohepatitis and cirrhosis. Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is now the most common cause of liver
disease in children. Although most patients with NAFLD are asymptomatic, laboratory abnormalities include elevations in levels of
liver transaminases (alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase), alkaline phosphatase, and gamma-glutamyl trans-
peptidase (Styne et al., 2017).

Musculoskeletal involvement
Childhood obesity increases the risk of various musculoskeletal problems including impairment in mobility, increased prevalence
of fractures, lower extremity joint pain, and lower extremity malalignment. Obesity is also a risk factor for unilateral or bilateral
slipped capital femoral epiphysis and for tibia vara (Kumar and Kelly, 2017; Styne et al., 2017).
